title: Can a circle show which crane's angle is bigger?
description: A transparent circle is placed on the first crane's angle with its centre on the vertex, and the arms cross its edge at A and B. The circle is moved to the second angle with one arm through A, and the point Y where the other arm crosses is compared with B. Keeko's doubt is that Y not sitting exactly on B means one angle is much bigger.
teaching_notes: One idea: on the same circle, the farther the second arm meets the edge from the first arm, the bigger the angle. Watch for students who think any small gap between Y and B means a big difference in the angles.

maths_rules: circle on the first angle: centre at the vertex O, the arms cross the edge at A and B
circle on the second angle: centre at the vertex, one arm through A, the other arm crosses the edge at Y
Y beyond B: the second angle is bigger; Y on B: equal; Y short of B: smaller
in the book's picture Y is very close to B, so the two angles are nearly equal (read from the picture)
slip: a tiny gap between Y and B means only a tiny difference between the angles
